task:
Author lane S1 of a two-lane independent measurement.
The full brief is `TASK.md` in your working directory. READ IT FIRST and follow it; this block only restates what is easiest to skip.
Everything you may read is under `bundle/`. That is deliberate and is the point of the exercise: a second lane is authored independently from the same bundle, and a third step compares the two. Do not look outside this workspace, and do not search for this project online. If you do read something outside it, say so in the attestation rather than leaving the field empty.
Read `bundle/docs/assurance/evidence/measurement/measurement-contract.md` before writing code. It is the specification; the summary in TASK.md is not.
Build: out/exporter.mjs runnable as `node out/exporter.mjs`, writes out/artifact.json out/artifact.json validates against bundle/.../artifact-schema.json, role: "lane" out/tests.mjs runnable as `node --test out/tests.mjs` out/NOTES.md what you implemented, what you decided, what you could not
The three things most likely to go wrong:
1. YOU choose the extraction policy (contract 4.2). The contract deliberately fixes no rule for binding one occurrence to another. Decide, implement, and then DECLARE what you implemented in the structured, digested form 4.5 requires — `parameters` must name every tunable you have.
2. EVERY in-scope anchor gets exactly one row (contract 4.3). The registry declares each relation's anchor domain. A missing row is a structural failure, not a silent pass. `ambiguous` is a legitimate result; a guessed binding is not.
3. Spans are byte offsets that must round-trip: decoding bytes[start:end] as UTF-8 must equal the literal you report (contract 3.5). Emit manifest paths verbatim — `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, not `bundle/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
Node 24 is available. No network, no dependencies.
structured_output_contract: Report at the end: 1. What extraction policy you implemented, and why you chose it over what you rejected. 2. Anchor counts you emitted per relation, per disposition. 3. Anything the contract left you unable to decide, and what you did instead. 4. Whether every span round-tripped, and how you checked. 5. Anything you read outside `bundle/`.
verification_loop: Before reporting done: node out/exporter.mjs node --test out/tests.mjs and verify out/artifact.json against the schema with a check you write. For every test you wrote, ask whether it would still pass if the behaviour it names were deleted; if it would, it is not testing that behaviour.
grounding_rules: Cite the contract clause for every design decision that the contract governs. Where you made a choice the contract leaves free, say so explicitly and label it as your judgment rather than as a requirement. Do not invent a binding you cannot justify from the bytes in front of you.
